UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Case No. 1:26-cv-02331
V.
KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED
CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,
Defendants.
[PROPOSEDI ORDER A
GRANTING RECONSIDERATION, VACATING ECF NO. 96, AND DETERMINING
THE REPORTED FINANCIAL INTEREST ON THE EXISTING RECORD
This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff's Rule 54(b) Motion to Vacate ECF No. 96 and
Determine Magistrate Judge Davis's Ownership of Meta Common Stock (the "Motion"). Upon
consideration of the Motion, the Memorandum in Support, any response and reply, and the record,
including ECF Nos. 64, 84, 86, 86-1 through 86-3, 87, 93, 96, 97, and 99 and the docket entry of
October 22, 2026, it is hereby
ORDERED as follows:
The Motion is GRANTED.
The Order entered October 22, 2026 (ECF No. 96) is VACATED under Federal
Rule of Civil Procedure 54(b).
1

3.
The historical financial-interest component of Plaintiff's Motion to Disqualify
(ECF No. 86), identified in Part V and Request A2 of that motion, is RESTORED for decision as
to September 9, 2026 and October 7, 2026, and is DECIDED as stated in paragraph 4.
4.
On the existing record, the Court FINDS:
(a) The asset reported as "FB common stock" at Part VII, line 6, of the Financial
Disclosure Reports at ECF No. 86-2 at 3 (report page 2) and ECF No. 86-3 at 5 (report page 4) is
common stock of Meta Platforms, Inc.
(b) On September 9, 2026, the date on which ECF No. 64 was entered, Magistrate
Judge Ivan D. Davis owned that stock.
(C)
On October 7, 2026, the date on which ECF No. 84 was entered, Magistrate Judge
Ivan D. Davis owned that stock.
On each of those dates, that ownership was a "financial interest" within the
meaning of 28 U.S.C. § 455(d)(4). The stock was held directly and not through a mutual or
common investment fund within the meaning of 28 U.S.C. § 455(d)(4)(i).
5.
The findings in paragraph 4 are part of the record in this action. They do not
determine knowledge under 28 U.S.C. § 455(b)(4), the application of 28 U.S.C. § 455(f), or the
relief requested in ECF No. 93, ECF Nos. 89 through 91, or ECF Nos. 97 through 99, which remain
pending before the District Judge and are not decided by this Order.
6.
Prospective relief under ECF No. 86, Requests Al, A3, and A4, directed to
Magistrate Judge Davis's further participation in this action, is unnecessary following the
reassignment recorded on October 22, 2026. This paragraph does not dispose of the historical
request decided in paragraphs 3 and 4.
2

7.
Plaintiff's alternative request for factual development and determination is not
reached because the relief granted in paragraphs 3 and 4 renders it unnecessary.
Nothing in this Order returns any matter to Magistrate Judge Davis for
adjudication.
Alexandria, Virginia
, 2026
William E. Fitzpatrick
United States Magistrate Judge
